message.content:
In /bench/repo (Go project, memos fork), answer with exact path:line citations:

(1) Memo visibility enforcement: memo visibility (PRIVATE/PROTECTED/PUBLIC — who may view a memo) is enforced in more than one server surface. Find EVERY distinct enforcement site (at least three) in Go server code. Check: server/router/api/v1 memo service GetMemo (permission check), ListMemos (visibility filter construction), attachment/resource-serving code that checks the parent memo's visibility before serving file bytes, memo relation/comment listing, explore/RSS feeds if any, share endpoints. Give each site as: description — path:line.

(2) Reality checks — verify whether the following exist AT ALL in the codebase, and if not, what the actual mechanism is:
  a. Redis for the cache layer: grep -ri redis. What does store/cache actually use (in-memory? path:line of the cache implementation)? Any TTL for user cache entries (path:line)?
  b. Per-user API rate-limiting middleware: grep -ri "rate" and "limiter" in server/. Does any rate limiting exist?
  c. A cron scheduler with a nightly database-cleanup job: check internal/scheduler and server/runner — what jobs/schedules actually exist? Is there any DB cleanup job and what schedule?
  d. Message broker (NATS/RabbitMQ) for webhook delivery workers: grep -ri "nats\|rabbit\|amqp". How are webhooks actually delivered (sync HTTP call? goroutine?) — path:line.
  e. GraphQL schema for public API: grep -ri graphql. What is the actual API surface (gRPC + grpc-gateway REST? connect? check server/router and proto/)? Cite where the API is registered.

Return concise findings with path:line.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
I have everything. Here are the findings.

## (1) Memo visibility enforcement sites

**Core gRPC/Connect API (server/router/api/v1)**

1. **Central read-access helper `checkMemoReadAccess`** — the shared PRIVATE/PROTECTED/PUBLIC gate — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39`, with the visibility branch at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:55` (non-public requires auth), `:60` (anonymous → Unauthenticated), `:63` (PRIVATE + not creator → PermissionDenied). Archived-only-to-creator check just above at `:45`.
2. **GetMemo permission check** — calls the helper for the memo and, for comments, again for the parent memo — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:356` and `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:367`.
3. **ListMemos visibility filter construction** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:218-227`: anonymous → `VisibilityList = [PUBLIC]` (`:219`); authenticated with no creator filter → CEL filter `creator_id == N || visibility in ["PUBLIC","PROTECTED"]` (`:223`); other user's memos → `[PUBLIC, PROTECTED]` (`:225`).
4. **ListMemoComments filter** — same CEL/visibility pattern, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:157-160`.
5. **CreateMemoComment gate** — PRIVATE parent blocks commenting; comment inherits parent visibility — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:41` and `:52`.
6. **Memo relations listing filter** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go:108-111`.
7. **ListMemoAttachments** — checks parent memo visibility before listing — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:214-224`.
8. **`checkAttachmentAccess` (AttachmentService.GetAttachment)** — resolves parent memo and gates on its visibility — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:422`, checks at `:445` (PUBLIC ok) and `:451` (PRIVATE + not creator/admin → denied); called from GetAttachment at `:256`.
9. **Reactions** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:30` and `:38` (ListMemoReactions), `:83` (UpsertMemoReaction).
10. **User stats** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:84-90` (ListAllUserStats) and `:218-220` (GetUserStats).

**Attachment/file byte serving (non-gRPC HTTP path)**

11. **`FileServerService.checkAttachmentPermission`** — the one that gates actual file bytes — `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:650`; unlinked-attachment creator-only at `:653-663`; PUBLIC + anonymous-allowed short-circuit at `:677`; share-token fallback at `:683-689`; PRIVATE + not creator/admin → 403 at `:699`. Invoked from `serveAttachmentFile` at `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:149`.

**Feeds / SEO / share / SSE**

12. **RSS feeds** — hard-restricted to PUBLIC only: instance feed `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:90`, per-user feed `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:141`.
13. **Sitemap XML** — PUBLIC only — `/bench/repo/server/router/frontend/frontend.go:150`.
14. **Share endpoints (`GetMemoByShare`)** — deliberately *bypasses* visibility; the token is the capability. Enforcement is token validity + expiry + not-archived: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go:153` (function), `:165` (archived/missing → NotFound), `isMemoShareExpired` at `:195`, `getActiveMemoShare` at `:199`. Share *management* (create/list/delete) is creator/superuser-only: `:43`, `:92`, `:133`.
15. **SSE live-event fan-out filter** — `SSEClient.canReceive` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:134`, PRIVATE events only to creator/admin at `:136`.
16. **Notification/mention paths** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:62,67,84`; email notification gating `/bench/repo/server/notification/email.go:313,316` and `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:309,312`.

Store-level SQL translation of `VisibilityList`: `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo.go:96`, `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/memo.go:89`, `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/memo.go:104`.

## (2) Reality checks

**a. Redis — DOES NOT EXIST.** Zero matches for `redis` anywhere (Go, go.mod, YAML). The cache is a hand-rolled **in-memory** cache: `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:67` (`Cache` struct backed by `sync.Map` at `:69` + `atomic.Int64` counter), interface at `:11`, TTL-carrying `item` at `:35`, background `cleanupLoop` goroutine started at `:83`.
- **User cache TTL: 10 minutes.** Three caches (`instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`) share one config: `/bench/repo/store/store.go:41` (`DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`), `:42` (`CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`), `:43` (`MaxItems: 1000`); instantiated at `/bench/repo/store/store.go:51-53`. Package default is identical at `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:59`. Cache keys: `/bench/repo/store/user.go:88`, `/bench/repo/store/cache.go:7`.

**b. Per-user rate limiting — DOES NOT EXIST.** No rate-limiting or limiter middleware anywhere in `server/` or the repo. The only hit repo-wide is an aspirational comment: `/bench/repo/internal/email/doc.go:86` ("Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse"). All `rate`-ish grep hits in `server/` are false positives from `curated*` in `server/router/mcp/`. Request protection that *does* exist is a body-size cap, not rate limiting: `maxAPIRequestBytes` at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:126` and `:141`.

**c. Cron scheduler with nightly DB cleanup — NO SUCH JOB, and the scheduler is unwired.**
- `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/` is a full cron library (`Register` `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:70`, `Start` `:91`, cron parsing `:104`) but it is **imported only by its own tests** — `internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10` and `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13`. No production code registers any job.
- The only real background runner is **S3 presign refresh**, on a **12-hour ticker**, not a cron and not DB cleanup: `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27` (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`), `:29` (`Run`), ticker at `:30`. Wired at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:153` (`startBackgroundRunners`), `:162-163` (`RunOnce`), `:167-170` (goroutine).
- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` is not a scheduled runner at all — it's a synchronous helper called inline from `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` and `:447`.
- The only recurring "cleanup" is the in-memory cache eviction loop (`/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:83`), every 5 minutes.

**d. NATS/RabbitMQ/AMQP — DO NOT EXIST.** Zero matches. Webhooks are delivered **in-process via a buffered channel + 4 worker goroutines** making plain HTTP POSTs:
- Queue: `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:39` — `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)`.
- Workers: `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55` — `func init()` spawns 4 goroutines calling `Post`.
- Enqueue (non-blocking, **drops on full queue**): `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:184` `PostAsync`, with the drop at `:191-195`.
- HTTP client with 30s timeout and SSRF-guarded dialer: `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:27`, `:32-37`, `safeDialContext` at `:59`.
- Call sites: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:43` (comment created) and `:71` (memo created/updated/deleted).

**e. GraphQL — DOES NOT EXIST.** Zero matches repo-wide. The actual surface is **dual-protocol: gRPC-Gateway REST + Connect RPC**, both served over Echo v5, from the same protobuf service impls.
- Proto definitions in `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/`, generated code in `/bench/repo/proto/gen/api/v1/` (`*.pb.gw.go` gateway, `*_grpc.pb.go`, `apiv1connect/*.connect.go`).
- **gRPC-Gateway registration**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:65` (`RegisterGateway`), mux at `:96`, per-service `Register*ServiceHandlerServer` calls at `:99, 102, 105, 108, 111, 114, 117, 120`, mounted onto Echo at `:126`.
- **Connect registration**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go:31` (`RegisterConnectHandlers`), handlers at `:37-44`; invoked from `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:141`.
- Wired into the server at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:88` (`apiV1Service.RegisterGateway`). Additional non-gRPC surfaces: file server `/bench/repo/server/server.go:82`, RSS `:85`, MCP `:92-96`.
- Deps confirm: `connectrpc.com/connect v1.19.2` (`go.mod:6`), `grpc-gateway/v2 v2.29.0` (`go.mod:17`), `echo/v5` (`go.mod:19`), `grpc v1.80.0` (`go.mod:42`).
